uncited: The method modifies the standard splatting pipeline by separating the projection of raw density from the computation of color and opacity.
**Sheet Buffer:** An image-aligned buffer storing the accumulated density contributions.
Unlike axis-aligned buffers that store slices of the volume, this buffer stores the projected footprints of all voxels in the current view direction.
This creates a "fuzzy" density field on the screen.
**Compute Screen Gradients:** Calculate the gradient of the projected density field on the screen.
**Classify and Shade:** Perform per-pixel classification and shading using the computed screen gradients.
Let $D(x,y)$ be the density value at screen coordinate $(x,y)$ accumulated in the sheet buffer.
The magnitude $|\nabla D|$ determines the edge strength.

*   **Pre-shaded + Post-classification Artifacts:** Combining pre-shaded voxel projection (where color is baked into the splat) with post-classification (setting pixels to zero if density is below threshold) causes severe artifacts.
*   **Sheet Buffer Alignment:** Post-classified rendering requires image-aligned sheet buffers.
*   **Performance Overhead:** The calculation of screen gradients and per-pixel shading adds overhead compared to pre-shaded splatting.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires an image-aligned sheet buffer.
